answer:
**Generative models trade off representation, likelihood, coverage, and sampling work in different ways.** A VAE learns an encoder and decoder through a likelihood bound, often enabling quick sampling and latent inference. A GAN learns through a discriminator and can generate sharp samples in one pass but may omit modes. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00028)

Normalizing flows use invertible transformations with tractable density calculations, constraining architecture while enabling exact likelihood under the model. Diffusion models learn iterative denoising or related dynamics and often provide strong quality and diversity at greater sampling cost. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239)

**No single metric captures the tradeoff.** A model can create attractive images while missing rare categories, or assign useful likelihoods while producing less visually sharp samples. Compare coverage, perceptual quality, inference needs, and end-to-end latency on matched data and resolution.

Distillation, latent representations, and fewer-step samplers can move the frontier. These are empirical tendencies, not a theorem that only three properties can ever coexist or that one family always wins. Choose based on the task's required outputs and budget, and include the cost of all encoding, iterative steps, and decoding.

**Technical details and references.**

VAEs offer fast amortized encoding and typically fast decoding with a likelihood lower bound, but likelihood/objective and decoder choices can trade detail for coverage. GANs often sample sharply in one generator pass but can miss modes and are difficult to train. Normalizing flows provide exact likelihood and invertible maps, with architectural constraints and speed depending on the flow. Diffusion models often combine strong quality and diversity at the cost of iterative sampling. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.00028) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239)

These are tendencies, not an impossibility theorem with a fixed winner. Distilled diffusion, consistency-style methods, latent representations, and autoregressive or continuous flows shift the frontier. Compare matched data, compute, resolution, quality/coverage metrics, and end-to-end latency. High perceptual quality is not synonymous with calibrated likelihood or complete mode coverage.
